title: Utilization of visualized patient education in dentistry
summary:
Visual aids are intended to help patients better understand medical information and feel more satisfied with the information they receive.
Students can also benefit from this, as images and illustrations facilitate learning and boost confidence during patient consultations.
Initial studies in periodontology suggest that audiovisual education can be helpful. Therefore, this study investigates whether standardized, tablet-based education improves patients’ understanding, satisfaction, and cooperation compared to conventional verbal or written education.
This is being investigated prior to periodontitis therapy and root canal treatment as part of dental education.

interventions.name: Intervention group: Patients receive visualized information.
Control group: Patients receive standard verbal and written information.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients: scheduled systematic periodontal therapy or scheduled primary root canal treatment; treatment takes place as part of a student course (IK I through IV); capacity to consent and voluntary written consent; sufficient knowledge of German to understand the informed consent form and questionnaires

Students: Participation in the clinical course (semesters 7–10), voluntary written consent, no prior participation in a comparable interventional study
Exclusion criteria:
Patients: lack of informed consent or capacity to consent; relevant pre-existing conditions affecting cognitive function; acute systemic diseases that preclude the respective dental treatment; insufficient knowledge of German (non-German speakers are excluded to ensure a consistent basis for communication); participation in another study affecting communication or patient perception; pregnancy

Students: Non-participation in the respective clinical course; lack of informed consent
